cards.h: India between the Guptas and the Sultans
cards.b: From the 7th to the 12th century power lay with regional kingdoms. The Cholas built the best local government and a sea empire. Historians argue over “feudalism” and the nature of the state.

For control of Kannauj, three powers fought from the 8th to 10th century: the Gurjara-Pratiharas (west and north), the Palas of Bengal (Dharmapala, Devapala; patrons of Nalanda, Vikramashila) and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan (Dantidurga; Krishna I built Kailasa at Ellora; Amoghavarsha). Arab travellers praised the Rashtrakuta king as one of the great kings of the world.

From the 8th century many clans rose: Chauhans (Ajmer; Prithviraj III lost to Muhammad of Ghor at the Second Battle of Tarain, 1192), Paramaras (Bhoja of Dhar), Chandelas (Khajuraho), Solankis or Chalukyas of Gujarat (Dilwara, Modhera), Gahadavalas (Kannauj), Kalachuris. Features: clan loyalty, forts, land grants, hero stones, patronage of Sanskrit. Mahmud of Ghazni raided from 1000 to 1027 (Somnath, 1025-26); Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-ul-Hind.

Founded by Vijayalaya (c. 850 CE), who took Thanjavur. Rajaraja I (985 to 1014): conquered the Cheras, Pandyas, north Sri Lanka, Maldives; built the Brihadisvara temple. Rajendra I (1014 to 1044): Ganga expedition; Gangaikonda Cholapuram; naval expedition against Srivijaya (c. 1025). Navy and overseas trade with Southeast Asia and China.

• Empire divided into mandalams, valanadus, nadus and villages (ur).
  • Uttaramerur inscriptions (Parantaka I, 919 and 921 CE): rules for electing village committees by lot (kudavolai), with eligibility rules (land, age, learning).
  • Assemblies: ur, sabha (Brahmin villages), nagaram (merchants).
  • Land survey and revenue (kaniyatchi); temple as economic centre; devadana, brahmadeya.

Trade guilds: Manigramam, Ayyavole 500, Nanadesi. Iron and textiles; ports: Nagapattinam, Mamallapuram. Society: Brahmins, Vellalas; devadasis. Temples: Brihadisvara, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, Airavatesvara. Bronzes (Nataraja). Literature: Kamban’s Ramavataram, Sekkizhar’s Periya Puranam. Cholas declined after Kulottunga III (13th century) to Pandya and Hoysala.

• Chalukyas of Badami (Pulakeshin II defeated Harsha, 630; Aihole inscription by Ravikirti), Eastern Chalukyas (Vengi).
  • Pallavas (Mahendravarman I, Narasimhavarman I; Mahabalipuram).
  • Pandyas (Madurai).
  • Hoysalas, Yadavas, Kakatiyas (Warangal; Rani Rudrama Devi).
  • Eastern Gangas (Konark), Palas, Senas.

cards.h: Indian feudalism and the segmentary state
cards.b: R. S. Sharma (Indian Feudalism, 1965) argued that land grants created feudalism and decline of towns after the Guptas. B. D. Chattopadhyaya and others reject it. Burton Stein (Peasant State and Society in Medieval South India, 1980) proposed the segmentary state: the Chola king had ritual power while local bodies held real power. Others, such as Y. Subbarayalu, point to the strong Chola bureaucracy.

Uttaramerur is cited as an early example of local democracy and of electoral rules. Cholas’ sea power is part of India’s Indian Ocean narrative; a Chola-style “Sengol” was placed in the new Parliament in 2023 (May). Rajput memory shapes Rajasthan’s heritage tourism and its politics.
